chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I love that Allah should know that I have humbled my neck in maintaining kinship ties, and I hasten to visit my family before they become self-sufficient of me.'

key_terms.أَصِلُهُمْ: I maintain ties with them / I visit them
key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِي: My family / people of my house
key_terms.لَأُبَادِرُ: I hasten / I rush to do
key_terms.يَسْتَغْنُوا عَنِّي: They become self-sufficient of me / no longer need me

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of hastening to visit family before they become self-sufficient?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the Shia virtue of *silat al-rahim* by emphasizing proactive humility, ensuring he serves his kin before their need for him diminishes. This hadith underscores the spiritual merit of initiating kindness rather than waiting for reciprocity, a practice deeply rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's model of selfless service. Such early engagement strengthens familial bonds and reflects a sincere devotion to Allah through social responsibility.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Dawood Bin Farqad who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would love it for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> to Know that I<sup>asws</sup> have humbled my<sup>asws</sup> neck regarding my kinship and I<sup>asws</sup> hasten to my<sup>asws</sup> family members to helping them before they become self-sufficient of me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 25. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following: “

Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said to me, ‘I love to show Allah humbling of my neck for my relatives and that I hasten to do good to my relatives and maintain good relations with them before they become independent of me.’”
